title: Chapter 2938 - 172: Yin and Yang
content:
Chapter 2938: Chapter 172: Yin and Yang

The Twelve Scripture Gluttonous Spirit Corpse Extremist Formation, uses the Twelve regular meridians within the cultivator’s body—Hand and Foot Taiyin, Jueyin, Shaoyin, Taiyang, Yangming, Shaoyang—as the core framework.

Using the bloodline in the main meridians as points, the veins as lines, the spirit as energy, the blood as essence, and organs as artifacts, from the outer skin, to flesh, to bone, adhering to the divine craftsmanship of creation, complex and precise, yet naturally harmonious, it connects the entire body, eventually merging into one.

The flesh and blood body born from heaven and earth, now seems like a "human machine" constructed by the Great Dao.

At this moment, Mo Hua’s custom-made "formation instrument" is following the procedure he planned, piercing silver needles delicately into his flesh along the acupoints of his limbs.

These silver needles simultaneously connect to his Twelve regular meridians.

The essence of Wood White and the marrow of golden jade, these two heavenly materials and earthly treasures, also infiltrate Mo Hua’s meridians along the silver needles as prearranged by Mo Hua.

The first to infiltrate is the marrow of golden jade.

The marrow of golden jade, belonging to the element of metal, fluid like jade, once inside the body, infiltrates downward from the flesh to settle onto Mo Hua’s bones.

Mo Hua’s bones have already nurtured the foundation of "Wood White Gold Jade" beforehand.

Now the marrow of golden jade precisely completes the final step of fusion, wrapping around Mo Hua’s strut bones, as if "gilding" his bones.

After the "gilding," the marrow of golden jade will not solidify within a few hours.

This stage is the only time to "engrave the formation."

At this moment, the essence of Wood White, mixed with wooden energy, half-clear and half-white, slowly infiltrates Mo Hua’s body along the silver needles.

The essence of Wood White contains vitality, instantly merging upon meeting blood, impossible to perceive.

Without perception, it cannot be controlled by Divine Sense.

Therefore, Mo Hua pre-mixed a bit of the Great Wilderness’ "blood poison" into the essence of Wood White.

This blood poison will also merge with the blood, but will induce a very distinct pain.

As long as there’s distinguishable "pain," Mo Hua can perceive it.

If perceptible, Divine Sense can "recognize" it.

If Divine Sense can recognize it, Mo Hua can manipulate the essence of Wood White to use it as "Spiritual Ink," to inscribe the Taotie Array on his bones.

Additionally, the blood poison itself has a certain "corrosive" property, able to corrode bones.

In this way, by using the poison itself instead of a "carving knife," one can leave traces of the formation on their bones.

This is the "poison engraving" method that Mo Hua pondered for a long time before conceiving.

No need to cut open the flesh, dissect the limbs, or "expose bones," but can use Divine Sense Control Ink to inscribe formation patterns on intact bones within the body.

As for the blood poison itself, although it can "corrode" bones, its toxicity is mild and not particularly harmful.

Mostly, it only corrodes the "gilded" surface of the bone.

Subsequently, the essence of Wood White naturally heals, and will conveniently clear away the blood poison, leaving no trace.

All processes are within Mo Hua’s "plan," and after countless deductions, confirmed error-free before he implements it.

Silver needles pierce into the Twelve meridians, the essence of Wood White blends into the blood. But because it’s mixed with "poison," causing pain, it’s easily "recognized" by Mo Hua’s Divine Sense.

Mo Hua begins to manipulate the essence of Wood White according to the Formation Diagram of the Twelve Scripture Gluttonous Spirit Corpse Extremist Formation, starting from the Hand Taiyin Lung Meridian, merging from blood into meridians, from meridians into networks, and after connecting the networks, inscribing the first stroke of the Taotie Spirit Formation Pattern on the radial side of the corresponding thumb.

The essence of Wood White merges blood into ink, falling on the bone "gilded" by the marrow of golden jade.

Sketching out the first stroke of the savage Taotie Formation Pattern.

This Taotie Pattern, once the first stroke lands, it’s as though a fierce beast bites the radial bone of the thumb, with pain penetrating the marrow.

Even though he has taken "Mashen Grass," and also gilded his bones with the marrow of golden jade.

Yet the pain still feels like maggots on a bone, penetrating the Mashen Grass and golden jade bone, branding itself onto Mo Hua’s Divine Sense.

This pain is neither of flesh nor of bones.

More like a "Law" pain.

It is the "mortals" of flesh who, audaciously attempt to use their own bones to bear the Law of Taotie Evil Spirits, and thus suffer the "backlash" pain.

This pain can penetrate all superficial defenses, directly impacting the "Divine Soul" itself.

Mo Hua also feels, bodiless unnamed fierce beasts tear into him, unbearable pain, with even his bones, meridians, and flesh beginning to tremble.

Fortunately, before inscribing his Life Formation, he "nailed" his flesh dead.

Otherwise, moving about would result in unimaginable consequences.

But the chains and shackles, deeply tightened into Mo Hua’s flesh, leaving significant blood bruises and marks on his pale hands and feet.

This is pain from the flesh, but it’s inconsequential.

The real pain is still suffering from the "Taotie" Law pain.

And this pain is intensifying.

The Taotie’s tearing is deepening.

This pain brought by a single stroke of formation pattern surpasses the limit that any ordinary cultivator can endure.

Even Mo Hua finds it unbearable and can only actively mobilize powerful divinity to suppress his humanity.

Placing his life, his flesh, his Sea of Consciousness, all of his pain... completely disregarded.

Using divinity to overlook all his sufferings as a human.

Deities are indifferent, treating all lives as straw dogs.

Mo Hua himself is one of the lives.

He considers himself as a "straw dog," placing all his sorrows and sufferings on the straw dog.
